messages:
sam_sales: Heads up — ACME's demo is flaking during their ramp. They report lots of 5xxs when they hit ~180rps sustained. Need a fast path to get the demo back.
tess_eng: can you share the error text? 502/503/504? Is it model OOM or upstream?
nora_support: stack shows mix of 502 + connection errors to our cache: "ERR connection pool exhausted" and some model timeouts reported. Started ~15:07 UTC and peaked for ~3m.
sam_sales: their script: 6 clients at ~30rps, prompts ~900 tokens, and they turned on client prefetch of cached completions.
ben_oncall: prefetch + high concurrency often multiplies backend KV lookups. If those are synchronous it will saturate conn pools and block runtime threads.
matt_sre: pulled perf traces — we see request queue depth spike to ~600, many requests waiting on KV. Autoscaler requested nodes ~30s after spike but new pods registered ~1m later.
tess_eng: so two issues: sync prefetch causing many parallel KV calls, and autoscale reaction latency. Immediate mitigations?
ben_oncall: quick options:
- ask customer to disable prefetch (immediate)
- apply per-route concurrency cap (we can set concurrency=40 for their demo route)
- temporarily increase redis maxclients and connection pool on model pods (ops change, but doable)
- fallback to smaller model shard that does fewer KV ops

sam_sales: ACME wants to keep prefetch if possible because it reduced p99 in small tests — but agrees to disable if we can recover demo fast. Also asked whether prefetch causes higher billing. they think more requests = more tokens but unsure.
nora_support: for billing: prefetch can increase request count and internal compute; so yes it can increase usage-based cost depending on how client implemented it. I'll confirm with billing.
deploy-bot: route-change-queue: request queued id=rchg-317, target=acme-demo-route, cap=concurrency:40
matt_sre: applied route cap. telemetry: queue depth dropping, redis wait errors decreasing.
ben_oncall: customer turned off prefetch at 15:10:35 UTC — success rate improved. Still seeing a few 502s during drain.
tess_eng: what about autoscaler? we should consider faster scale-up for short spikes. Suggest lowering target CPU threshold for demo pool and shorten stabilization window.
matt_sre: can make a temporary aggressive policy for the demo pool (scale cooldown 20s, ramp faster). I'll open ops change and keep it short-lived.
sam_sales: ACME back on, demo proceeding. They asked for a writeup of follow-ups before tomorrow's exec sync.
ben_oncall: follow-ups we recommended:
- client: adopt async prefetch (non-blocking) or use server-side batched prefetch so single KV call per request when possible
- SRE: increase redis conn pool and consider pipelined prefetch implementation
- Infra: investigate autoscaler responsiveness for spikey demo workloads and add a fast-path policy for POC/demo routes
- Docs: note prefetch caveat under "High concurrency" patterns and add guidance on cost impact
- Sales: confirm pricing impact with billing team (Nora) and update ACME.

nora_support: billing: prefetch that triggers extra requests will count toward usage charges; however dedup/caching approaches can reduce net load if implemented server-side. I'll confirm numbers with billing and send ACME an estimate.
tess_eng: I'll file eng-ticket ENG-2207 for async prefetch pattern and ENG-2208 to detect sync-prefetch anti-patterns at runtime (warn customers).
matt_sre: filed SRE-891 for redis pool sizing and SRE-892 for autoscaler tune.
sam_sales: great. I'll close the loop with ACME and request exec demo replay if needed. Thanks all. :tada:
